title: Handler leaks
key_conclusions: Handler leaks are retained-path problems through Thread, Looper, MessageQueue, Message, callback, target, or obj rather than a generic Handler-class problem.
Delayed messages extend the lifetime of captured Activity, Fragment, binding, or View objects until execution or explicit removal.
The correct cancellation boundary must match the victim lifecycle: Activity onDestroy, Fragment View onDestroyView, or HandlerThread owner disposal.
A Handler leak fix should be accepted only with before/after evidence from LeakCanary, HPROF Path To GC Roots, dumpsys meminfo, thread state, or source-path verification.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative retained paths rather than a real target-app HPROF.
It does not decode a real LeakCanary Handler trace line by line with concrete class names.
It does not validate Handler, MessageQueue, Looper, and Message method names against a specific Android branch checkout.
It does not include a live MessageQueue dump or custom instrumentation proving which delayed Message remained queued.
